hypotheses: The variables X_1,...,X_N are independent (PDF page 7, printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 opening; PDF page 8, printed page 19, derivation of (2.7)).
Each X_i is Bernoulli with parameter p_i, hence its exponential moment appearing in (2.7) is finite (PDF pages 7-8; printed pages 18-19, theorem opening and the MGF computation after (2.7)).

The selected parameter lambda is strictly positive, so multiplication by lambda and exponentiation preserve the event S_N>=t in the direction used by exponential Markov (PDF page 8; printed page 19, first and final proof paragraphs).
Within the enclosing theorem, t>mu (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 statement).

definitions_and_conventions: S_N denotes the uncentered sum sum_{i=1}^N X_i (PDF page 7; printed page 18, Theorem 2.3.1 statement).
E exp(lambda X_i) is the moment-generating function of coordinate X_i evaluated at lambda (PDF page 8; printed page 19, paragraph immediately after (2.7)).

The product ranges over every coordinate i=1,...,N, and each expectation is taken under the same underlying probability law (PDF page 8; printed page 19, equation (2.7), structurally inherited from the common independent family).
The event boundary is non-strict, S_N>=t, and the comparison to the right side is also non-strict (PDF page 8; printed page 19, equation (2.7)).
The exponential prefactor is exp(-lambda t), not exp(-lambda mu) and not a centered-tail factor (PDF page 8; printed page 19, equation (2.7)).
implicit_context: Equation (2.7) is a proof step inside Theorem 2.3.1 rather than a separately quantified proposition; its X_i, S_N, mu, and t come from the enclosing theorem (PDF pages 7-8; printed pages 18-19, theorem statement followed by proof).

The derivation repeats the method leading to equations (2.5) and (2.6) in the proof of Hoeffding's inequality: exponential Markov followed by MGF factorization (PDF page 8, printed page 19, first proof paragraph; PDF page 3, printed page 15, equations (2.5)-(2.6)).

Although the X_i are Bernoulli in the enclosing theorem, the form of (2.7) uses only their independence and existence of the displayed exponential moments; Bernoulli structure is used in the next paragraph to bound each factor (PDF page 8; printed page 19, equation (2.7) and following paragraph).

The notation X_1,...,X_N and product from i=1 to N conventionally treats N as a finite positive integer, but no separate N>=1 hypothesis is printed (PDF pages 7-8; printed pages 18-19, theorem statement and (2.7)).

The threshold t remains the theorem's fixed but arbitrary value above mu; (2.7) does not introduce a new threshold quantifier (PDF pages 7-8; printed pages 18-19, theorem statement and proof).

contract_plain_english: Inside the proof of Chernoff's inequality, let S_N be the sum of the enclosing independent Bernoulli variables and let t be the theorem's threshold above its mean. For every positive exponential parameter lambda, the probability that S_N is at least t is at most exp(-lambda t) times the product, over i=1 through N, of the individual moment-generating functions E exp(lambda X_i). The prefactor comes from exponential Markov and the product comes from independence. Equation (2.7) ends at this exact product; the Bernoulli-specific estimates of its factors occur only afterward.
